proposed.explanation: None of these movements attempted to return to classical principles; they pursued forward-looking abstraction. Ornament rejection was ideological, not economic; all three pursued philosophy over pragmatism. The three movements used distinctly different formal languages: orthogonal (De Stijl), asymmetrical (Constructivism), sculptural (Expressionism). This precisely captures the article's core teaching: all three rejected ornament and tradition, but pursued abstraction toward different ends—De Stijl toward universal principles, Constructivism toward revolutionary power, Expressionism toward emotional response.
